questions.text: What do you do? Do you work or study?
questions.say: Good afternoon. My name is Lewis, and I'm your examiner today. This is the Speaking test. In this first part, I'd like to ask you some questions about yourself. Let's talk about what you do. What do you do? Do you work or study?

questions.text: What was your favourite subject at school, and is it useful to you now?

questions.text: What do you find most rewarding about your work or your studies?

questions.text: What is the hardest part of your work or studies?
questions.say: What is the hardest part of your work or studies?

questions.text: Where did you go to primary school?
questions.say: Now let's move on to talk about primary school. Where did you go to primary school?

questions.text: What do you remember about your first teacher?
questions.say: What do you remember about your first teacher?

questions.text: What did you enjoy doing at primary school?
questions.say: What did you enjoy doing at primary school?

questions.text: Do you mind being in crowded places?

questions.text: How do you feel when a bus or train is crowded?

cueCard.topic: Describe an invention that has changed the way people live.
cueCard.explain: and explain how it has changed people's lives.

questions.text: Describe an invention that has changed the way people live.
questions.say: Thank you. Now, in Part 2, I'm going to give you a topic, and I'd like you to talk about it for one to two minutes. Before you talk, you'll have one minute to think about what you're going to say. You can make some notes if you wish. Here is your topic. Describe an invention that has changed the way people live. You should say: what the invention is; when it was invented; how people use it; and explain how it has changed people's lives.

questions.text: Could you live without this invention?
questions.say: Thank you. Could you live without this invention?

questions.text: What is the most important invention of the last hundred years?
questions.say: Thank you. We've been talking about an invention that has changed the way people live, and I'd like to discuss with you some more general questions related to this. Let's consider first of all inventions. What is the most important invention of the last hundred years?

questions.text: Do all inventions make life better?
questions.say: Do all inventions make life better?

questions.text: Why do some inventions become popular while others are forgotten?
questions.say: Why do some inventions become popular while others are forgotten?

questions.text: Should governments spend more money on scientific research?
questions.say: Now let's talk about science and research. Should governments spend more money on scientific research?

questions.text: Why are fewer young people choosing to study science in some countries?
questions.say: Why are fewer young people choosing to study science in some countries?

questions.text: What do you think will be the next great invention?
questions.say: What do you think will be the next great invention?
